title: Sola fide means: not by law's perfect works, but by living efficacious faith
source_text: XXXII. Sed quum Scriptura dicit hominem justificari fide, & non operibus, seu sine operibus, quod nos dicimus sola fide justificari, sensus simpliciter est, neminem justificari posse praestando opera quae lex ab homine requirit, ut per eam justificetur: sed solum credendo in Christum fide viva & efficaci, quod postulat Evangelium, ut apud Deum pro justis habeamur. Per opera autem quae lex proprie sumpta, & ut opponitur gratiae, sive Evangelio, exigit ad hominis justificationem, intelligitur, perfecta & nullo unquam peccato interrupta, omnium mandatorum legis observatio, quae omnem transgressionem, & omne peccatum excludit. Lex enim dicit, Fac & vives, &, Qui fecerit ea vivet in eis. Maledictionem vero districte denunciat omnibus peccatoribus atque transgressoribus, dum ait, Maledictus omnis qui non permanserit in omnibus quae scripta sunt in libro legis hujus, ut faciat ea.
pass_a_gloss: But when Scripture says a person is justified by faith and not by works, or without works—which we call being justified by faith alone—the sense simply is that no one can be justified by performing the works the law requires of a person that he may be justified by it: but only by believing in Christ with living and efficacious faith, which the Gospel requires that we may be held as just before God. And by the works which the law properly taken, and as opposed to grace or the Gospel, requires for a person's justification, is understood the perfect observation of all the law's commandments, never interrupted by any sin, which excludes every transgression and every sin. For the law says, Do this and you shall live, and Whoever does them shall live by them. But it strictly denounces a curse on all sinners and transgressors when it says, Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all that is written in the book of this law, to do them.
pass_b_english: Sola fide: not law's uninterrupted perfect obedience, but living efficacious faith in Christ.
Law's justifying works = flawless observance—Fac et vives—or the curse.

lemmas.gloss: Do this and you shall live

rejected: without any good works at all
